top:
usage: ophiolite [-h] [--version] <group> ...

Start here:
  ophiolite demo --bundle PATH  A demo project on this computer, with three commands to try
  ophiolite account login       Approve this project in your browser
  ophiolite data wells list     The wells you may read, located
Groups:
  account   Sign in, check this computer, and who can see what
  data      Read what you may see: curves, wells, lists and exact revisions
  exchange  Bring files in and take bundles out
  results   Make, publish and follow results
  tools     Write, check and run your own tools
  starter   Starter packs of one catalogue record
  demo      A demo project on this computer, with three commands to try
Run 'ophiolite <group> --help' for its commands; 'ophiolite --version' for the release.

account.help:
usage: ophiolite account [-h] <command> ...

Sign in, check this computer, and who can see what

positional arguments:
  <command>
    login         Approve this project in your browser
    logout        Revoke application access
    status        Check application access
    doctor        Check local setup without running code or contacting the server
    projects      List the projects a credential reaches (no configuration or project needed)
    orgs          List the organisations holding a project the credential reaches
    teams         The teams: the project's (administrators), or an organisation's with
                  --organization (owners)
    access-history
                  Who had access to what, and when: the project's history (administrators) or one
                  person's (organisation owners), or a CSV or JSON Lines file
    ai-use        Whether your own work may be used for AI
    share         Give colleagues read or reuse access to a result or original you own
    audience      Who can see an uploaded original of yours and who can build on it: show it, or
                  change it in one step
    rights        The rights to use data: show them, or attach or renew them (project
                  administrators, or who added the original)

options:
  -h, --help      show this help message and exit

usage: ophiolite data [-h] <command> ...

Read what you may see: curves, wells, lists and exact revisions

positional arguments:
  <command>
    curves    A depth window of one exact curve for display: every sample (level 0) or blocks with
              their extrema
    wells     The wells you may read, located (list), or their extent; from-run RUN...: the wells

    fetch     Read an exact revision into a new local folder

    surveys   List the surveys you may see, with the members you may read

exchange.help:
usage: ophiolite exchange [-h] <command> ...

Bring files in and take bundles out

positional arguments:
  <command>
    import         Add a table file as wells, well tops, deviation surveys, point sets or time-
                   depth pairs: table FILE --target T (--dry-run to review), list, status ID,
                   pause ID, resume ID, cancel ID
    upload         Upload a file, a folder, a .zip or an https address: every file it can read is
                   added, and one report says what became of each
    export         Export exact revisions into a new portable bundle
    bundle         Check or summarize a portable bundle offline (no server or account needed)
    send           Send a file as a new item, or as the next version of one you hold; it is
                   private until you share it
    deliver        Deliver exact versions to a team's system with a send tool of the project, from
                   this computer
    intake         Read a file of an upload on this computer with a read tool of the project, and
                   send what it made
    source         Run a source tool of the project on this computer and add what it reads from a
                   team's system
    sources        Your upstream source selections: list them, describe one (costs one full read),
                   or read its rows
    repositories   Public repositories (NLOG): search SERVICE --name N, bring-in SERVICE CODE...
                   --audience P, check SERVICE [CODE...]
    well-imports   Import a copy of an approved well table as wells: list, status ID, start
                   (--dry-run to preview), resume ID, cancel ID
    sample         Start from the NLOG sample: one gamma-ray log and 2,222 wells (project
                   administrators)
    new-data       What new files start with in this project: who can see them, depth reference,
                   coordinate system, units and attribution
    templates      The table targets you can download a template for, their units and formats
    template       Download a template for a table target: its header in your units and one
                   example row the import skips
    targets        What each type of table needs: its fields, which are required and the choices
                   that describe it (offline)
    layouts        The project's layouts: list, show NAME, rename NAME NEW, retire NAME, use-again
                   NAME, export [NAME...] --out FILE, import FILE, keep CONNECTION TABLE, update
                   NAME, reconnect NAME CONNECTION TABLE
    org-connections
                   Your organisation's database connections that you use or administer, with your
                   own readiness

options:
  -h, --help       show this help message and exit

results.help:
usage: ophiolite results [-h] <command> ...

Make, publish and follow results

positional arguments:
  <command>
    prepare        Fetch exact input; no computation or publication
    run            Execute your prepared Python script on this computer
    publish        Publish the prepared result; does not share it
    correct        Run and explicitly publish the bounded offset example
    publish-derived
                   Publish a file you derived from exact revisions, with its declared method (a
                   command id or a work folder is required)
    remake         Make an exact result version again and compare; nothing is saved without --save
    recover        Recover a saved exact request from its private work folder
    withdraw       Withdraw one result version, with your reason (this also records that you
                   reject it)
    verdicts       Verdicts: whether you accept or reject one result version, and why
    outcomes       Outcomes: what this project accepts for residual results and where they are
                   delivered (administrators change them)
    story          How an exact result version was made: its inputs and their inputs, a page at a
                   time
    what-changed   What differs in how two exact result versions were made
    dependents     The results made from an exact version you may read
    trajectories   Your own work in a project as episodes a model may learn from
    try            What one request would do, kept nowhere (a dry run)

options:
  -h, --help       show this help message and exit

verbs.prepare: Fetch exact input; no computation or publication
verbs.run: Execute your prepared Python script on this computer
verbs.publish: Publish the prepared result; does not share it
verbs.correct: Run and explicitly publish the bounded offset example
verbs.publish-derived: Publish a file you derived from exact revisions, with its declared method (a command id or a work folder is required)
verbs.remake: Make an exact result version again and compare; nothing is saved without --save
verbs.recover: Recover a saved exact request from its private work folder
verbs.withdraw: Withdraw one result version, with your reason (this also records that you reject it)
verbs.verdicts: Verdicts: whether you accept or reject one result version, and why
verbs.outcomes: Outcomes: what this project accepts for residual results and where they are delivered (administrators change them)
verbs.story: How an exact result version was made: its inputs and their inputs, a page at a time
verbs.what-changed: What differs in how two exact result versions were made
verbs.dependents: The results made from an exact version you may read
verbs.trajectories: Your own work in a project as episodes a model may learn from
verbs.try: What one request would do, kept nowhere (a dry run)

tools.help:
usage: ophiolite tools [-h] [--json]
                       {new,validate,run,register,list,show,enable,withdraw,trust,verify,verifications,publish,again,sandbox,init,skills,checks,rules,residuals,recipes}
                       ...

positional arguments:
  {new,validate,run,register,list,show,enable,withdraw,trust,verify,verifications,publish,again,sandbox,init,skills,checks,rules,residuals,recipes}
    new                 Write a starting tool folder
    validate            Say whether Ophiolite would accept a tool folder, and why not
    run                 Run a tool on local files; writes its outputs and run.json into a new
                        folder
    register            Register a tool folder as a private version of this project
    list                The tools of this project you can see
    show                One tool: what it reads and makes, its settings and who registered it
    enable              Enable a version for everyone in this project (administrators)
    withdraw            Withdraw a version: it is never fetched or run again
    trust               Trust a version, so running it asks nothing
    verify              Verify a version against a passed check of a result it made or a published
                        method, or withdraw a verification
    verifications       Who verified a version, against what and when
    publish             Publish a run made with run --from-project on project versions (--input
                        SLOT=@RESULT:REVISION): each output once, under the run
    again               Run a tool-made result again on this computer; the project says whether it
                        is the same result
    sandbox             Run an enabled version in the project's sandbox: the server runs it and
                        publishes each output
    init                Start an application from a packaged template (map-application, derive-
                        and-publish, sync-worker, notebook, agent-workflow)
    skills              Locate packaged SDK guidance
    checks              Checks against a reference: publish, list, compare a result with a file,
                        and who may publish
    rules               Data rules: the results of the rules checked when a version landed, or on
                        a file on this computer
    residuals           Residuals at wells: run a residual tool on a well selection and a surface,
                        on this computer
    recipes             Run a recipe (the residual report again) step by step, and continue it
                        after a stop

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --json                Print the documented JSON result (errors as {"error": {...}})

verbs.validate: Say whether Ophiolite would accept a tool folder, and why not
verbs.run: Run a tool on local files; writes its outputs and run.json into a new folder
verbs.register: Register a tool folder as a private version of this project
verbs.list: The tools of this project you can see
verbs.show: One tool: what it reads and makes, its settings and who registered it
verbs.enable: Enable a version for everyone in this project (administrators)
verbs.withdraw: Withdraw a version: it is never fetched or run again
verbs.trust: Trust a version, so running it asks nothing
verbs.verify: Verify a version against a passed check of a result it made or a published method, or withdraw a verification
verbs.verifications: Who verified a version, against what and when
verbs.publish: Publish a run made with run --from-project on project versions (--input SLOT=@RESULT:REVISION): each output once, under the run
verbs.again: Run a tool-made result again on this computer; the project says whether it is the same result
verbs.sandbox: Run an enabled version in the project's sandbox: the server runs it and publishes each output
verbs.init: Start an application from a packaged template (map-application, derive-and-publish, sync-worker, notebook, agent-workflow)

starter.help:
usage: ophiolite starter [-h] [--json] {build,opendtect,python,resinsight,finalise,export} ...

positional arguments:
  {build,opendtect,python,resinsight,finalise,export}
    build               Land the inputs, then write starter.json (unpublished, no keys), its
                        fidelity document and the python target; the same command again continues
    opendtect           Run the pack's import.py into an existing OpendTect survey, read each
                        placed object back and compare it with the landed item at its pinned
                        version; writes files/targets/opendtect/result.json, then starter.json's
                        oracle
    python              Run the pack notebook on the pack folder with the network blocked; writes
                        files/targets/python/result.json, then starter.json's oracle; reads this
                        computer only
    resinsight          Run the pack's ResInsight import.py into a new project, read every well
                        path and log back through rips (again after reopening) and compare it with
                        the pack; writes files/targets/resinsight/result.json, then starter.json's
                        oracle
    finalise            Write each artefact's key from its held custody document; reads this
                        computer only
    export              Export a survey archive's cubes, horizons and wells with the OpendTect
                        connector, read them back and write derived.json; reads this computer only

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --json                Print the documented JSON result (errors as {"error": {...}})

verbs.build: Land the inputs, then write starter.json (unpublished, no keys), its fidelity document and the python target; the same command again continues
verbs.opendtect: Run the pack's import.py into an existing OpendTect survey, read each placed object back and compare it with the landed item at its pinned version; writes files/targets/opendtect/result.json, then starter.json's oracle
verbs.python: Run the pack notebook on the pack folder with the network blocked; writes files/targets/python/result.json, then starter.json's oracle; reads this computer only
verbs.resinsight: Run the pack's ResInsight import.py into a new project, read every well path and log back through rips (again after reopening) and compare it with the pack; writes files/targets/resinsight/result.json, then starter.json's oracle
verbs.finalise: Write each artefact's key from its held custody document; reads this computer only
verbs.export: Export a survey archive's cubes, horizons and wells with the OpendTect connector, read them back and write derived.json; reads this computer only
